Bundle: Full pre-registration sweep. Scope: cycle-1 audit of `pulitzer_prize_for_fiction_winners_2000_2024` using the cited source set first, with bounded Wiki-family source discovery.

Verdict: Not ready. The row universe, PK shape, source_count, `query_category=implicit_join`, and `operation_type=join` are structurally sound, but three exact-match cells are not registration-ready.

Findings

1. 2004 Edward P. Jones birth cell is wrong. (factual, BLOCKING)
- Staged CSV cell: `Author Birth State or Country = Virginia` for `2004 | Edward P. Jones | The Known World`.
- Cited ground-truth source: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_P._Jones`, infobox `Born` field and lead/early-life text. The article states Jones was born in `Washington, D.C., U.S.`; the same page says he was born in Washington, D.C. and raised there. Locator: infobox `Born`, plus `Early life and education` first paragraph.
- Why this blocks: the declared normalization rule is born-location, using `Washington, D.C.` as an allowed U.S.-born value. `Virginia` appears to have been pulled from education/employment context, not the birth field. This is an exact-match answer-key error.
- Recommended repair: change the CSV cell to `Washington, D.C.` and update all derived distribution/prose references: temporal_note, _extraction_notes, source_coverage_notes, normalization_decisions, and decision_log should list Washington, D.C. as 3 rows (Chabon, Jones, Greer) and remove Virginia from the birth-state distribution.

2. 2010 Paul Harding birth-state cell is not grounded by the cited source. (factual, BLOCKING)
- Staged CSV cell: `Author Birth State or Country = Massachusetts` for `2010 | Paul Harding | Tinkers`.
- Cited ground-truth source: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Harding_(author)`, infobox `Born` field and `Life and career` section. The infobox gives only `Born 1967`; it does not state a birth place. The body says Harding `grew up` in Wenham, Massachusetts, which supports a raised/location association, not the declared born-location field. Locator: infobox `Born`; `Life and career` first paragraph.
- Why this blocks: the instance claims the implicit-join cell is derived from the per-author article's `Born` field and that raised-in locations are not used. The cited source does not support Massachusetts as a birth state under that rule.
- Recommended repair: either add a source that explicitly grounds Harding's birth state and update `source_urls`, `source_count`, and source-role prose, or change the cell/rule so the answer is not represented as a source-grounded birth state. If the curator keeps `Massachusetts`, the source plan must explicitly cite the extra source and distinguish born-vs-raised evidence.

3. 2022 Joshua Cohen book title is not verbatim from the master winners table. (factual, BLOCKING)
- Staged CSV cell: `Book = The Netanyahus` for `2022 | Joshua Cohen`.
- Cited ground-truth source: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Fiction`, winners table, `1980s to present`, 2022 row. The master table's `Work` cell is `The Netanyahus: An Account of a Minor and Ultimately Even Negligible Episode in the History of a Very Famous Family`.
- Why this blocks: draft/curation prose repeatedly says `Book` is verbatim from the master Pulitzer winners table. The staged cell is the shortened/common title, not the table value. Exact-match evaluation will treat this as a different answer.
- Recommended repair: change the CSV cell to the full master-table work title, or explicitly change the normalization rule to use per-book canonical short titles and add a source that supports that choice. The simpler repair is to use the full master-table title.

Passed checks

- Universe/cardinality: the cited master winners table supports 25 staged rows for the 2000-2024 window after excluding the 2012 no-award row and adding the 2023 co-winner row. Current 2025 and 2026 winners are correctly documented as outside the staged window.
- Composite PK: `(Year, Author)` is unique and handles 2023 co-winners plus Colson Whitehead's two in-window wins.
- Source count: `source_count = 25` matches `len(source_urls) = 25` (1 master + 24 distinct author pages).
- Metadata: `query_category = implicit_join`, `operation_type = join`, `claim_type = source_defined`, and `domain = Culture/Literature` are consistent with the protocol and domain taxonomy.
- Heterogeneous column design: `Author Birth State or Country` honestly names the mixed U.S.-state/DC vs foreign-country value rule; no separate scope finding on Variant A.
- Sort: CSV is sorted by `Year`, with the 2023 tie ordered by full displayed `Author` field (`Barbara Kingsolver` before `Hernan Diaz`).
- Wiki-family discovery: no alternate Wiki-family source was found that changes the row universe. The master Pulitzer page is the right universe source; the only source-set defect found is value-level grounding for Paul Harding's birth state.

Counts

Severity counts: 3 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION.
Issue-type counts: 3 factual, 0 structural, 0 scope-related.

Minimal repair list

1. Change Edward P. Jones birth value from `Virginia` to `Washington, D.C.` and update distribution prose.
2. Ground or revise Paul Harding's `Massachusetts` birth-state cell; the cited Wikipedia article only supports grew-up-in Massachusetts, not born-in Massachusetts.
3. Change Joshua Cohen's book cell to the full master-table title, or document and source a short-title normalization rule.

Registration judgment: Not ready until the three blocking exact-match/source-grounding issues are repaired.
